snippet.title: IVF Supplements: What Really Helps? CoQ10, DHEA, Vitamin D & More
snippet.description:
Which supplements actually help with IVF? Dr Senai Aksoy, Associate Professor of Reproductive Medicine, checks the usual bottles (folic acid, vitamin D, CoQ10, myo-inositol, melatonin, antioxidants, NMN and DHEA) against one question: did the studies count babies?

In short: no supplement has been shown to give women more babies with IVF. Folic acid is for almost everyone, to protect the baby. Vitamin D, if your level is low. CoQ10 is a "maybe" for low ovarian reserve. DHEA probably makes little or no difference to live births.

📖 Full article with all sources: https://draksoyivf.com/blog/coq10-melatonin-nac-oocyte-quality-ivf/

CHAPTERS
00:00 Which supplements actually help with IVF?
00:59 How do we know a supplement works?
01:55 The Evidence Score (0 to 4)
02:53 Folic acid
03:41 Vitamin D
04:46 CoQ10: the one "maybe"
06:14 Myo-inositol
06:59 Melatonin
07:36 Antioxidant blends and NAC
08:17 NMN
08:40 DHEA
09:40 Before you add another bottle
10:40 My take
11:04 Recap and 3 questions for your doctor

EVIDENCE SCORE (Dr Aksoy's teaching scale, not an official score: how close has the evidence come to more babies?)
4 · good trials, more babies: none
3 · better eggs, embryos or pregnancy rates, not more babies: CoQ10 (low reserve)
2 · small or low-quality, uncertain: vitamin D (for IVF results), myo-inositol, melatonin, antioxidant blends/NAC
1 · lab or animal only: NMN
0 · tested in randomized trials, probably no difference in births: DHEA
Not scored: folic acid (different job: protecting the baby)

QUESTIONS TO ASK YOUR DOCTOR
1. Based on my tests, does any supplement make sense for me, and why?
2. Is anything I'm taking now unnecessary, or could it interfere with my treatment?
3. Should my vitamin D level be checked?

SOURCES
• USPSTF 2023, folic acid 400–800 µg: https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2023.12876
• Chu 2018, vitamin D and IVF (observational): https://doi.org/10.1093/humrep/dex326
• Zhou 2022, vitamin D trials in deficient women: https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2022.852428
• Xu 2018, CoQ10 RCT, low reserve under 35: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12958-018-0343-0
• Florou 2020, CoQ10 meta-analysis: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10815-020-01906-3
• Lin 2024, CoQ10 meta-analysis: https://doi.org/10.1080/07853890.2024.2389469
• Bentov 2014, CoQ10 placebo-controlled trial (stopped early): https://doi.org/10.4137/CMRH.S14681
• ESHRE 2023, add-ons in ART: https://doi.org/10.1093/humrep/dead184
• ESHRE 2025, ovarian stimulation guideline: https://doi.org/10.1093/humrep/deag018
• Zhang 2025, myo-inositol meta-analysis: https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2025.1520362
• Retracted: Papaleo 2008 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2008.01.088 · Pacchiarotti 2016 https://doi.org/10.3109/09513590.2015.1101444
• Fernando 2018, melatonin placebo-controlled RCT: https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2018.00545
• Showell 2020, Cochrane review of antioxidants (editorial note 2026): https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007807.pub4
• Bertoldo 2020, NMN in older mice: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.01.058
• Naik 2024, Cochrane review of DHEA and testosterone: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD009749.pub3
• ASRM 2024, smoking and fertility: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2023.12.029

MEDICAL INFORMATION
This video is for education and information only. It is not personal medical advice, a diagnosis or a treatment recommendation. Do not start or stop any supplement or medication without your own doctor.

LANGUAGE AND PRODUCTION
The English voice in this video was generated with AI from Dr Aksoy's own voice, and lip movements in the scenes where he is on camera were adjusted with AI to match the English audio. Supporting footage is illustrative (stock footage and AI-generated visuals). No supplement brand is shown or endorsed.
